blocks.text: I can explain how to multiply a 3-digit number by a 2-digit number.
We will use three steps to make a big multiplication easier.
Tap the word to see what it means.

items.def: Any of the multiplication results we get leading up to an overall multiplication result is a partial product.

blocks.text: Example: 16 × 4.

items: Add them: 40 + 24 = 64. This is the overall product.

blocks.text: There are 31 seats in each row and there are 29 rows. How many seats altogether?
This is a multiplication: 31 × 29. We can show it in a grid (area) model.
The grid model shows that each row has 31 seats and there are 29 rows.
To make multiplying easier, we can partition the smaller number. The smaller number is 29.
There are still 31 seats in each row, but now we partition 29 rows into 20 rows and 9 rows.
Both multiplications are easier to calculate. We are trying to be more efficient.
Look at 58 × 34. The smaller factor is 34.

blocks.q: How do we partition the smaller factor, 34?
blocks.why: 34 is 30 and 4, so the calculations are 58 × 30 and 58 × 4.

blocks.text: A part-part-whole model can show the same strategy. The whole is 31 × 29. The parts are 31 × 20 and 31 × 9.
These are the partial products.

items: 31 × 2 = 62, and 20 is 10 times the size, so 31 × 20 = 620.

blocks.label: So how many seats?
blocks.text: 31 × 29 = 899. There were 899 seats in the section.
Now 43 × 22. We partition 22 into 20 and 2.
43 × 22 = 946. There were 946 seats.

blocks.q: Use partitioning to find the missing number in each pair of expressions.
Match each multiplication to the two multiplications you get when you partition the smaller factor.

blocks.text: A stall stocks 232 bottles of water on each shelf. It has 17 full shelves. How many bottles?
This is 232 × 17. The grid model shows that each shelf has 232 bottles and there are 17 shelves. We partition the smaller number, 17, into 10 and 7.

items: 232 × 10 = 2,320. This is the first partial product.
232 × 7 = 1,624. This is the second partial product.

blocks.text: There are 3,944 bottles altogether.
There are 23 seats in each row and 341 rows. This is 23 × 341. We partition 23 into 20 and 3.
You can use a grid model or a part-part-whole model to show your thinking.
Andeep drew a grid for 245 × 33. He partitioned 33 as 3 and 3.

blocks.label: Tap to see what went wrong
blocks.text: 33 was partitioned incorrectly. The grid should show 30 and 3, so the calculations are 245 × 30 and 245 × 3.

blocks.q: For 402 × 22, which two partial products do we add?
Partition the smaller number, calculate the partial products and add them.

blocks.text: We can use informal methods of multiplication to calculate the product.

items: Add the partial products to recombine.

blocks.text: Remember: partition the smaller number so the calculations are easier.

flashcards.back:
Any of the multiplication results we get leading up to an overall multiplication result.

16 × 4: the partial products are 40 and 24.

flashcards.front: What are the three steps to multiply using partitioning?
flashcards.back:
1) Partition one of the factors.
2) Calculate the partial products.
3) Add the partial products to recombine.

flashcards.back: 31 seats in each row. There are 29 rows.

flashcards.back: 40 (4 × 10) and 24 (4 × 6). Add them to get the product, 64.

232 × 17: partition 17 and give the two partial products.

flashcards.back: 30 and 3, so the calculations are 245 × 30 and 245 × 3.

worksheet.instructions: Partition the smaller factor, calculate the partial products and add them to find each product. Write your answer as a number.

245 × 33 is partitioned into 245 × 30 and 245 × 3. What is the partial product 245 × 30?
questions.explanation: 245 × 3 = 735, and 30 is 10 times the size, so 245 × 30 = 7,350.
